title: Autopsy and Ledger
premise: True-crime podcaster Jonah Nakamura has built a quiet reputation solving deaths the police mislabeled as accidents, but when twin letters arrive — one confessing to a forty-year-old drowning, one promising a second death at an upcoming anniversary dinner — he realizes the writer knows his methods intimately. Following a coded ledger hidden in the victim family's estate records, Jonah uncovers a pattern of inheritances laundered through staged accidents, implicating the very family hosting the anniversary dinner. As the dinner approaches, Jonah must decide whether justice means exposure or something the law cannot deliver, and in the end he lets the confession air publicly while allowing the dying patriarch's chosen heir — the letter-writer herself, a disinherited daughter — to walk free, choosing belonging over legal victory.
about_author: O. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former estate paralegal who spent a decade cataloguing wills, trusts, and the quiet resentments they leave behind. They write mysteries about paper trails and the people who bleed through them.

chapters.title: The Coldest Case
chapters.summary: Jonah Nakamura, POV. Recording the finale of his podcast season on a 1983 drowning ruled accidental, Jonah reflects on the three deaths he's quietly solved and the loneliness of knowing things no court will hear. The beat is restless triumph — success that tastes like unfinished business.

chapters.title: Twin Letters
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. Two envelopes arrive the same morning: one a detailed confession to the 1983 drowning, signed only 'L,' the other promising 'a second glass raised' at the Vane family's fortieth anniversary dinner. The emotional beat is vertigo — his work has summoned him into someone else's design.

chapters.title: What the Police Missed
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV, with flashback interludes. He verifies the confession against coroner records and finds details only the killer could know — yet the letter also contains one deliberate error, a test. Beat: wary respect for an adversary who studies him back.

chapters.title: The Vane Estate
chapters.summary: Jonah travels to the coastal town of Port Merrow, POV. He surveys the Vane mansion where the anniversary dinner looms in three weeks and meets estate archivist Ruth Okafor, who guards the family papers. Beat: the uncanny feeling of being expected.

chapters.title: Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. She shows Jonah the family's ornate household ledgers, which patriarch Edmund Vane insists on keeping by hand; certain entries repeat in odd sequences. Beat: dawning recognition that the accounting itself is a cipher hiding transfers of inheritance.

chapters.title: A Death Called Accident, Again
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. He matches ledger anomalies to a second death — a 1991 boating accident that benefited Edmund's late brother. The pattern holds: every anomaly precedes a death that consolidated wealth. Beat: cold dread hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Dinner Invitations
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. A formal invitation to the anniversary dinner arrives — addressed before he ever contacted the family. He accepts, telling himself it's research. Beat: the seduction and danger of being welcomed by suspects.

chapters.title: The Heirs
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, vignette-style. Introductions to the Vane heirs: brittle eldest son Marcus, charming granddaughter Celeste, estranged daughter Lena presumed abroad, and gentle second wife Iris. Beat: a family performing unity over fault lines.

chapters.title: Error as Signature
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. He realizes the deliberate error in the confession mirrors an error in the ledger — both point to the same date, Lena Vane's birthday. Beat: the hunter realizing the hunted may be an ally, or bait.

chapters.title: Ruth's Silence
chapters.summary: Ruth, POV. Pressured by Marcus to restrict archive access, Ruth hesitates, then secretly copies three ledger pages for Jonah. Her chapter reveals she suspected the pattern years ago and stayed silent out of loyalty. Beat: guilt choosing a side.

chapters.title: The Second Letter Fulfilled
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. A near-fatal fall from the estate's cliffside stairs injures Iris days before the dinner — ruled another accident. Jonah finds the scene staged exactly as promised. Beat: fury; the promise was kept, and he arrived too late.

chapters.title: Hospital Glass
chapters.summary: Iris, POV. Recovering, Iris tells Jonah she recognized her attacker's cologne but refuses to name them, hinting the family's rot predates Edmund. Beat: complicity and tenderness entangled — she protects someone Jonah needs exposed.

chapters.title: Decoding the Ledger
chapters.summary: Jonah and Ruth, alternating POV. Working through the night, they crack the cipher: repeated entries encode dates, beneficiaries, and payments to a fixer. Every death maps to a transfer. Beat: exhilaration curdling — the ledger proves everything and names no living hand.

chapters.title: Marcus Moves First
chapters.summary: Marcus, POV. Sensing scrutiny, Marcus confronts Jonah, offers money to drop the podcast season, then threatens him with trespass charges. Beat: the banality of menace — power accustomed to buying outcomes.

chapters.title: Lena Returns
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. The disinherited daughter comes home early, ostensibly for the dinner, and meets Jonah in the chapel ruin where her mother drowned. Their conversation is a duel of half-truths. Beat: two investigators circling the same wound.

chapters.title: The Fixer's Grave
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. He traces the fixer named in the ledger to a pauper's grave and a surviving widow who confirms decades of payments — and one final job scheduled for the night of the dinner. Beat: countdown pressure; the next death has a date.

chapters.title: Confession, Second Draft
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Lena admits she wrote the letters: she found the ledger after Edmund's stroke and has been forcing the family's history into the open, but swears she never intended harm. Jonah believes her — mostly. Beat: trust extended on a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The dinner unfolds in full: toasts, veiled accusations, Jonah present as guest and witness. When the third glass is raised, the lights fail — the fixer's move begins. Beat: elegance stretched over panic.

chapters.title: The Third Glass
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV. In the darkened house, Jonah intercepts the attack meant for Edmund, unmasking the fixer and, behind him, Marcus — who inherited not just money but method. Beat: climax; physical danger resolving into moral clarity.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Jonah, Lena, Ruth, POV rotation. Marcus is arrested on the ledger evidence; Edmund, lucid for one hour, acknowledges his crimes and dies before dawn. Jonah airs the full story but omits Lena's letters. Beat: grief braided with a chosen mercy.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Lena, POV. Lena declines the estate, signing it toward the staff and a memorial fund, and asks Jonah to help her record the victims' real stories. Beat: belonging rebuilt from what remains rather than what was taken.

chapters.title: Season Four
chapters.summary: Jonah, POV, epilogue. Months later, Jonah launches a new season opening with the Vane case solved and closes with a fresh envelope on his desk — this time postmarked from his own hometown. Beat: peace interrupted by invitation; the ledger continues.
